orientation.01:
Before we begin…

This deck is generated by over 3,000 lines of code
and I felt it deserved seven cards for orientation.

(You can delete or suspend these cards so they don't appear again.)

⟪cloze⟫
orientation.02:
Grammar words might fry your brain:
What's the second person plural of the perfect tense for 'dar'?

Huh?

Instead, the deck drops you
right in the middle of the sentence
and gives you visual cues:

↧ En aquel momento, de repente, ↧
vosotros […dar…]


⟪cloze⟫
orientation.03:
For beginners, the idea behind the deck is that
you learn all Spanish conjugation in one go.

Even before you start properly studying Spanish, if you like!

This is an amazing language-learning hack.
The manual explains why.

⟪cloze⟫
orientation.04:
For advanced learners, you can filter the deck
(using extremely specific tags)
in order to drill down on a specific part of Spanish conjugation.

⟪cloze⟫
orientation.05:
During normal usage you'll just
swipe left or right (if on mobile.)

But when you are confused about a verb form or curious to learn more
the card shows lots of extra details.

⟪cloze⟫
orientation.06:
I hesitated to include the
↬ Subjunctive Future ↬

You rarely hear it except in expressions such as

adonde fueres haz lo que vieres
(~ when in Rome, do as the Romans)

…and in speeches or comedies in rural settings…

⟪cloze⟫
orientation.07:
If you see something that could improve
(bugs, stats, tags, idioms)

please write to me.

By the way if you'd like different colors, each element has its own css style
which you can change in Anki.

But enough talking already.

⟪cloze⟫
